subject: maths
question: Two cyclists start simultaneously from points X and Y, which are 150 km apart, and head towards each other. They meet after 3 hours. If the speed of one cyclist is 25 km/h, what is the speed of the other cyclist?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of cyclists moving towards each other = Total Distance ÷ Time

Relative speed = 150 ÷ 3 = 50 km/h

Speed of the other cyclist = Relative speed − Speed of one cyclist

Speed of the other cyclist = 50 − 25 = 25 km/h

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between X and Y = 150 km

Time taken to meet = 3 hours

Speed of first cyclist (S₁) = 25 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (towards each other) = S₁ + S₂

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = (S₁ + S₂) × Time

⇒ 150 = (25 + S₂) × 3

⇒ 150 ÷ 3 = 25 + S₂

⇒ 50 = 25 + S₂

⇒ S₂ = 50 − 25

⇒ S₂ = 25 km/h

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Average Speed

Average speed for a round trip with speeds a and b is (2 × a × b) ÷ (a + b).</p
